subject.title: resolveCliAuthEpoch invalidates every live CLI session when local credential source-of-storage flips, even though identity is unchanged

question: For Claude CLI sessions with an auth-profile credential present, should the auth epoch treat local credential file/keychain source presence as identity-changing, or should the auth-profile identity be canonical for session continuity?
rationale: Current code deliberately treats local credential absence as meaningful auth-state loss, but the report shows that same rule also invalidates live sessions when only the local source of storage appears or disappears.

options.title: Prefer auth-profile identity
options.body: Skip the local Claude CLI fingerprint whenever a selected auth-profile credential is present, and rely on auth-profile identity changes to invalidate sessions.

options.title: Keep storage-sensitive epochs
options.body: Leave local credential presence in the epoch and accept same-identity session resets when the non-prompting local read flips between null and readable.

options.title: Add explicit backend ownership mode
options.body: Define a narrower CLI backend auth-owner contract before changing Claude CLI so profile-owned, host-owned, and mixed modes each have upgrade tests.

recommendation.title: Prefer auth-profile identity
recommendation.body: Skip the local Claude CLI fingerprint whenever a selected auth-profile credential is present, and rely on auth-profile identity changes to invalidate sessions.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant auth invalidation behavior and follow-up CLI continuity work trace most strongly through this history.
